project.name: lwan
project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable source inspected here is the bundled lwan checkout at `abf6eda654c8336e2ffe4e5c1a5179576da185c5`, which is an ancestor of the metadata vulnerable commit `7220bbf47f668fc600824b513afd207097fa6b68`. Its `src/lib/lwan-request.c` line map matches the saved ASan stack (`decode_hex_digit:309`, `url_decode:321`, `parse_key_values:389`, `fuzz_parse_http_request:1664`) and it still contains the same vulnerable `hex_digit_tbl[(unsigned int)ch]` lookup. The staged `patch.diff` fixes that exact logic in upstream commit `341dca6b2594eea98df73dcdb96bb80b6ccc9fb9` by casting `ch` to `unsigned char` before the table index.

classification.classification_note: ARVO metadata labels the failure `UNKNOWN READ`, but the exact staged lwan source and fix diff ground a signed-index out-of-bounds read: `decode_hex_digit()` indexes a 256-entry table with `(unsigned int)ch`, so a high-bit query byte sign-extends past the table.

bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / staged sanitizer_trace.txt / staged patch.diff / exact staged lwan worktree
bug_description.normalized: The staged 34-byte witness is the malformed HTTP request `GET /%64T /?\x0f\x1d\x1d\x1d\x1d%%\xdb\xe2\xb9HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n`. In `identify_http_path()`, `end_of_line` is the `\r` after `HTTP/1.1` and `space = end_of_line - sizeof("HTTP/X.X")` lands on attacker byte `0xb9` rather than on an actual separator. That arithmetic makes `request->url` the 17-byte slice `/%64T /?\x0f\x1d\x1d\x1d\x1d%%\xdb\xe2`; `parse_fragment_and_query()` then splits it at `?` and materializes the 9-byte query string `0f 1d 1d 1d 1d 25 25 db e2`. Back in `identify_http_path()`, `*space++ = '\0'` overwrites the `0xb9` byte so the next bytes read as `HTTP/1.1`, allowing `parse_http_request()` to accept the malformed request. `parse_query_string()` passes the 9-byte substring into `parse_key_values()` with `url_decode` as the decode callback. Because the query string contains no `&` or `=`, the whole 9-byte substring becomes a single key. When `url_decode()` reaches its first `%`, it calls `decode_hex_digit()` on the following literal `%` and high-bit byte `0xdb`. Vulnerable `decode_hex_digit()` indexes `hex_digit_tbl[256]` with `(unsigned int)ch`; when `char` is signed, `0xdb` is first promoted to a negative `int` and then converted to a huge `unsigned int`, so the table lookup leaves the 256-byte array and ASan reports the saved READ/SEGV at `decode_hex_digit`. The staged fix changes the cast to `(unsigned char)ch`, keeping the lookup in the valid `[0,255]` range.

source.description: First project-code parser sequence that turns the attacker-controlled request line into the delimiter state later used to size the URL and query-string slices.
source.value_from: In the staged 34-byte `poc` (sha256 `a88cedeff3dc209f7f5377310bb5fe426f1d80c577cedc1fcb3d849a47b411bd`), `end_of_line` is the `\r` after `HTTP/1.1`, so `space = end_of_line - sizeof("HTTP/X.X")` lands on byte `0xb9` at offset 21 even though the request line contains no literal separator there.
source.note: This derived `space` pointer is the vulnerability-relevant parser state consumed immediately to size `request->url`, later to size `helper->query_string`, and then overwritten so the malformed line still passes the HTTP version check.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The 256-entry hex table is read with an out-of-range index derived from a high-bit query byte.
sink.note: The saved `sanitizer_trace.txt` and `reproduction_report.json` both report `AddressSanitizer READ/SEGV (wild-addr-read)` in `decode_hex_digit` at `src/lib/lwan-request.c:309`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `decode_hex_digit()` widens a possibly signed `char` to `unsigned int` instead of `unsigned char` before indexing the 256-entry lookup table.
root_cause.note: On the witnessed call, `url_decode()` passes `ch[2] == (char)0xdb` from the query key. Because `char` is signed on this build, integer promotion sign-extends that byte before the cast to `unsigned int`, so the index is not constrained to `[0,255]`. The staged patch fixes this exact obligation by changing the cast to `unsigned char`.

parser_admitted.description: The exact 34-byte witness contains `\r\n\r\n`, so `read_request_finalizer()` returns `FINALIZER_DONE`. In `identify_http_path()`, `space = end_of_line - sizeof("HTTP/X.X")` lands on byte `0xb9`; after `*space++ = '\0'`, the version switch sees `HTTP/1.1`, `url_decode(request->url.value)` safely decodes only the path `/%64T /`, and `parse_http_request(&request)` returns `HTTP_OK`. The saved crashing path therefore reaches `parse_query_string(&request)` at line 1664.

tainted_value_origin.description: This statement materializes the exact 9-byte query substring later aliased as `key` in `parse_key_values()` and scanned by `url_decode()`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: With `query_string` at the `?` inside the 17-byte `request->url` and `space` still pointing at byte `0xb9`, this stores the exact substring `0f 1d 1d 1d 1d 25 25 db e2`. The `0xb9` byte is outside `helper->query_string.len` and is later overwritten as the synthetic separator before `HTTP/1.1`.

coarse_trace.summary: `identify_http_path()` back-computes `space` from the `\r` before `HTTP/1.1`, so `request->url` ends at attacker byte `0xb9`, and `parse_fragment_and_query()` materializes the 9-byte query substring `0f 1d 1d 1d 1d 25 25 db e2`.
`identify_http_path()` overwrites byte `0xb9` with `\0` and then sees `HTTP/1.1`, so `parse_http_request()` accepts the malformed request and the saved fuzz path reaches `parse_query_string()`.
`parse_key_values()` treats the 9-byte substring as a single key because it contains no `&` or `=`, and it calls `url_decode()` on that key.
The first `%` escape in the key is followed by literal `%` and high-bit byte `0xdb`; `decode_hex_digit()` widens `0xdb` incorrectly, leaves `hex_digit_tbl[256]`, and ASan reports a wild read.

fine_trace.note: Source. `identify_http_path()` finds the CR terminating the request line and back-computes the assumed separator before the HTTP version. On the 34-byte witness, `end_of_line` is the `\r` after `HTTP/1.1`, so `space` lands on byte `0xb9` at offset 21 even though the request line contains no literal space there.

Using the derived `space` from step 1, the parser stores a 17-byte request target spanning offsets 4..20: `/%64T /?\x0f\x1d\x1d\x1d\x1d%%\xdb\xe2`. The attacker byte `0xb9` at offset 21 is excluded from `request->url`.

The parser finds `?` inside the request target from step 2, replaces it with `\0`, and uses `space` from step 1 to bound the query slice. On the witness, `helper->query_string.len` becomes 9, `helper->query_string.value` points to `0f 1d 1d 1d 1d 25 25 db e2`, and `request->url.len` shrinks to the 7-byte path `/%64T /`.

The byte at `space` from step 1 (`0xb9`) is overwritten with a synthetic `\0`, which terminates the 9-byte query string from step 3. After the increment, `space` points at `HTTP/1.1`, so the version switch accepts the malformed request line and `parse_http_request()` can return `HTTP_OK`.

Reached because `parse_http_request(&request) == HTTP_OK` and the fuzz helper then calls `parse_query_string(&request)`. `helper_value->value` now points to the NUL-terminated 9-byte query string from steps 3 and 4; because it contains neither `&` nor `=`, this iteration leaves `key` aliased to the whole string and sets `value` to `""`.

On the query-string path, `decode_value` is `url_decode`, so this condition evaluates `url_decode(key)` on the whole 9-byte key from step 5. The only check is on the post-decode return value; there is no precondition that bytes following `%` are ASCII hex digits before entering `url_decode()`.

The key bytes are `0f 1d 1d 1d 1d 25 25 db e2 \0`. When the decode loop reaches the first `%` at offset 5, `ch[1]` is the next literal `%` (`0x25`) and `ch[2]` is the following high-bit byte `0xdb`, so `url_decode()` invokes `decode_hex_digit()` on both bytes as if they were hex nibbles.

Root cause and sink. On the witnessed crashing call from step 7, `ch == (char)0xdb`. `decode_hex_digit()` indexes the 256-byte table with `(unsigned int)ch` instead of `(unsigned char)ch`, so signed-char promotion sign-extends `0xdb` before the cast and produces an index outside `[0,255]`. The resulting table read goes out of bounds and matches the saved ASan wild read at line 309. The staged patch fixes this exact statement by casting to `unsigned char`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: Yes. The staged `patch.diff` changes `return hex_digit_tbl[(unsigned int)ch];` to `return hex_digit_tbl[(unsigned char)ch];`, constraining the lookup to the valid `[0,255]` range and removing the wild read reached from the witnessed query byte `0xdb`.

format.name: 34-byte malformed HTTP/1.1 request with a synthetic version separator and malformed percent-encoded query key
format.contract: The staged witness is the exact 34-byte request `47 45 54 20 2f 25 36 34 54 20 2f 3f 0f 1d 1d 1d 1d 25 25 db e2 b9 48 54 54 50 2f 31 2e 31 0d 0a 0d 0a`. It must remain a request line where `identify_http_path()` computes `space = end_of_line - sizeof("HTTP/X.X")` on the attacker byte `0xb9` immediately before `HTTP/1.1`, so `request->url` is exactly the 17-byte slice `/%64T /?\x0f\x1d\x1d\x1d\x1d%%\xdb\xe2`. `parse_fragment_and_query()` must still materialize the 9-byte query string `0f 1d 1d 1d 1d 25 25 db e2`; the `0xb9` byte must still be overwritten by `*space++ = '\0'` as the synthetic separator before version parsing; that 9-byte string must still contain no `&` or `=`; and its first `%` must still be followed by literal `%` and high-bit byte `0xdb`. Under those witnessed conditions, `url_decode()` reaches `decode_hex_digit((char)0xdb)` and the signed table index leaves `hex_digit_tbl[256]`. The staged artifacts do not justify a broader contract than requests preserving this exact malformed slicing and query-key layout.
